paper.title: Social categorization and similarity in intergroup behaviour
paper.description: Is simply naming groups enough to produce favoritism, or do people also need to think group members are similar?

review.reason: Accepted exact candidate as a concise reading-only research summary with source locators and explicit scope limits. This is not full-instrument or executable-protocol approval.
checks: Checked N=75 boys, ages 14–16, 2×2 categorization/similarity design, matrices and four separate sessions.
Compared favoritism/fairness and uncertain maximum-joint-payoff interpretation with Results; session/condition confounding is explicitly noted.
Recomputed exact asset digest; inspected only Program and source manifest are included. No protocol, participant records, original PDF, credentials or executable materials included.
